wins.text: Q1 revenue of $26B, up 262% YoY and up 18% sequentially, well above the $24B outlook
Data Center revenue of $22.6B, a record, up 427% YoY and up 23% sequentially, driven by Hopper GPU demand
Non-GAAP gross margins expanded to 78.9% on lower inventory costs, with GAAP gross margins at 78.4%
Returned $7.8B to shareholders via share repurchases and dividends in Q1; announced 10-for-1 stock split and 150% dividend increase
Spectrum-X Ethernet networking solution ramping with multiple customers including a 100,000 GPU cluster; expected to become a multibillion-dollar product line within a year

risks.text: Data Center revenue in China is down significantly from pre-October export control levels; market expected to remain very competitive going forward
Gross margins guided to step down to 74.8% GAAP / 75.5% non-GAAP in Q2, with full-year expected in the mid-70s, a meaningful sequential compression from Q1's 78.9%
H200 and Blackwell supply constrained; demand expected to exceed supply well into next year, risking customer delivery delays
InfiniBand networking experienced a modest sequential decline in Q1 due to supply timing, though demand remained ahead of shipments
Cloud hyperscalers and large customers developing custom ASICs internally, representing potential long-term competitive pressure on GPU demand

guidance_items.detail: Q2 revenue guided to $28B +/- 2%, above Q1 actual of $26B and well above prior Q1 outlook of $24B; sequential growth expected across all market platforms
Q2 GAAP gross margin guided to 74.8% and non-GAAP to 75.5% (+/- 50 bps), down from Q1's 78.4%/78.9%; full-year expected in mid-70s%
Full-year OpEx expected to grow in the low 40% range; Q2 GAAP OpEx ~$4B, non-GAAP ~$2.8B
Sovereign AI revenue expected to approach high single-digit billions this year, up from near zero the prior year
Blackwell production shipments starting Q2, ramping Q3, with customer data centers stood up in Q4; significant Blackwell revenue expected this year

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential pause or digestion in Hopper/H100 demand as customers await Blackwell and H200 upgrades
Competitive threat from hyperscaler-developed custom ASICs and internal GPU programs
Supply allocation strategy between China-specific products (H20) and rest-of-world Hopper products
